title: The Hijra: Muhammad's migration from Mecca to Medina
summary: In 622 CE the Prophet Muhammad and his companion Abu Bakr left Mecca for Yathrib, about 320 km north, later called Medina, after persecution and a reported plot against him. Tradition places the first mosque at Quba. The year became year 1 of the Islamic calendar, chosen under Caliph Umar.

uncertainty.note: Lumen Learning gives June 622 CE for the migration; medinacity.net places arrival at Quba in September 622 CE (Rabi' al-Awwal, 1 AH). The sources differ, so only the year is relied on.

as_recorded.value: September 622 CE / Rabi' al-Awwal, 1 AH (arrival at Quba)

beats.caption: Muhammad and Abu Bakr leave Mecca for Yathrib, about 320 km north, after persecution and a reported plot.
After hiding and travelling by a coastal route, they reach Quba, where a mosque is founded.
The year of the migration becomes year 1 of the Islamic calendar, a choice made under Caliph Umar.
